# heytownhall_sso_domain (Resource)

An email domain that a single sign-on connection covers. People with an address at a verified domain sign in through the connection.

Creating the resource claims the domain but does not verify it. Publish `verification_record` in the domain's DNS, then confirm it with `heytownhall_sso_domain_verification`. `verification_record` is known as soon as the domain is created, so a DNS resource in the same configuration can use it (see the examples). A verified domain belongs to one organisation. The API refuses free-mail domains such as `gmail.com`.

Import with `<connection id>/<domain id>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "heytownhall_sso_domain" "acme" {
  connection_id = heytownhall_sso_connection.okta.id
  domain        = "acme.com"
}

# Publish this record in DNS, then confirm it with heytownhall_sso_domain_verification.
output "dns_record" {
  value = heytownhall_sso_domain.acme.verification_record
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `connection_id` (String) The id of the `heytownhall_sso_connection`. Changing it replaces the domain.
- `domain` (String) The email domain, in lowercase, such as `acme.com`. Write a non-ASCII domain as punycode. Changing it replaces the domain.

### Read-Only

- `domain_id` (String) The domain's id within the connection.
- `id` (String) `<connection id>/<domain id>`.
- `verification_record` (Attributes) The DNS record that proves control of the domain. It stays the same for as long as the domain is claimed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--verification_record))
- `verified_at` (String) When the API found the record (RFC 3339). Null until the domain is verified.

<a id="nestedatt--verification_record"></a>
### Nested Schema for `verification_record`

Read-Only:

- `name` (String) The full record name, such as `_heytownhall-verify.acme.com`.
- `type` (String) The record type. Always `TXT`.
- `value` (String) The record value, such as `heytownhall-verify=...`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by <connection id>/<domain id>.
terraform import heytownhall_sso_domain.acme 22222222-0000-4000-8000-000000000000/33333333-0000-4000-8000-000000000000
```
